newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B index hits yr low at noon, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index hits yr low at noon, seen steady.

text.p: Newcomer Bengang Steel Plates Co's sharp falls on Wednesday morning dragged down Shenzhen's B share index, but analysts said the index was likely to bottom out on the absense of major market-moving news.
The Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index slipped 2.29 points or 1.89 percent to 119.02 points, after hitting a low for 1997 of 118.78 points. Turnover was HK$26.3 million.
The A share index shed 1.78 points or 0.46 percent to 380.49 points. Turnover was 2.3 billion yuan.
"Bengang's plunge is having a strong negative impact on the market," an analyst at J&A Securities said.

The steel issue, which on Tuesday became the first new stock this year to close lower on its debut, dived HK$0.23 or 9.79 percent to HK$2.12. Analysts said investors were shunning China's ailing steel sector.
Bengang closed on Tuesday at HK$ 2.35 compared with the HK$2.38 offer price.
The failure of the July 1 Hong Kong handover to lift indices had shattered investor confidence in the market, analysts said.
Many had expected the territory's historic transition to Chinese from British rule to generate market euphoria.
"The indices are likely to stabilise in the near future as the recent falls have wiped out this year's gains," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"A lot of attention has been diverted to Hong Kong's red chips since the territory returned to the motherland," the J&A analyst said.
Red chips, Hong Kong shares with Chinese backing, have been a major focal point leading up to the former colony's handover.
On the A share market, Baiying Copper Commercial Building (Group) was the biggest loser and droped 0.33 yuan or 4.87 percent to 6.45 yuan.
